live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: ALPHV
next.headline: ALPHV (BlackCat): leak-site extortion, big data-theft claims and a casino phone-call intrusion
next.in_short: ALPHV, also called BlackCat, is a ransomware group known by several names. Reports describe leak-site extortion, large data-theft claims and a role in the 2023 casino attacks. Many figures are the group's own claims.

sentences.t: ALPHV is also tracked as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue record lists tools tied to the group. They include Mimikatz, PsExec, Impacket, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel.
SecurityScorecard says RansomHub is likely filling the vacuum left by the disbanding of AlphV/BlackCat and by law enforcement action against LockBit.
DataBreaches.Net reports that the group named a victim on its leak site. It then threatened to publish the data and spam the victim's customers.
In one reported case the group claimed to have stolen data without encrypting the victim's network. The report presents this as the group's own claim.
One report says a simple phone call was the way in for attacks on two Las Vegas casino operators. It says ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware then crippled their infrastructure.
In November 2023, DataBreaches.Net reports, the group listed Hampton-Newport News CSB, a community service board. It claimed over 800 GB of client and employee data and set a 48-hour deadline.

In July 2023, ransomware groups Clop and ALPHV (BlackCat) both listed cosmetics maker Estée Lauder as a victim. BlackCat claimed more than 130 GB of stolen data. The report says the scope of the attack was yet to be determined.

A separate report says Scattered Spider acted as an affiliate of ALPHV in the 2023 attacks on MGM and Caesars casinos. It also says Scattered Spider later used ALPHV/BlackCat, Qilin, RansomHub and DragonForce encryptors.
Treat a leak-site data-size claim as the group's own word until the victim or an independent party confirms it.
Staff who answer phones and handle help-desk requests are part of the defence. Train them to check who is calling.
